plots.title: Retrieval Precision@1 on Phase 6.1 Validation Set
plots.purpose: Compare first-result retrieval quality across lexical and semantic retrieval methods on the Phase 6.1 validation suite.
plots.description: Bar chart comparing top-1 precision (P@1) achieved by Baseline Lexical, BM25, CodeAware, and Semantic (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) on the multi-language validation test corpus (N=10 queries).
plots.dataset: Amoeba Multi-Language Retrieval Benchmark (7 elements, 10 queries)
plots.methodology: Evaluated across 10 query categories with 1 query per category. P@1 is 1.0 if the first returned result is relevant, 0.0 otherwise.
plots.notes: On this small 10-query validation set, semantic retrieval correctly handled the single conceptual query that lexical retrieval missed while matching lexical methods on the remaining categories.

plots.title: Ranking Quality Across Retrieval Methods
plots.purpose: Evaluate multi-depth ranking metrics across lexical and semantic retrieval pipelines on the validation set.
plots.description: Grouped bar chart displaying Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at 5 (NDCG@5), and NDCG@10 across all 4 retrieval methods on the validation set.
plots.methodology: Computed using standard logarithmic discounting (log2) for NDCG and reciprocal rank of first relevant item for MRR.
plots.notes: Semantic retrieval achieved 1.00 MRR and 0.997 NDCG on the validation set by eliminating rank demotion on conceptual queries.

plots.title: Retrieval Quality (P@1) by Category (1 Query per Category)
plots.purpose: Analyze performance tradeoffs across diverse developer query types.
plots.description: Horizontal grouped bar chart illustrating P@1 for each retrieval method broken down by 10 query categories (1 query per category, N=10 total).
plots.methodology: Queries are mapped to respective categories (1 query per category) and tested against identical ground truth relevance sets.
plots.notes: Lexical and BM25 achieve 1.0 on exact/identifier/path categories but 0.0 on the single Conceptual/Semantic query due to vocabulary mismatch. Semantic retrieval matches on exact and bridges the conceptual query.

plots.title: Retrieval Latency by Method
plots.purpose: Measure and compare core index lookup and ranking latency without embedding generation overhead.
plots.description: Bar chart comparing retrieval execution time in milliseconds across Baseline Lexical (0.02ms), BM25 (0.04ms), CodeAware (0.08ms), and Semantic cosine scan (<0.01ms median).
plots.methodology: Measured over repeated query executions in C++ engine and vectorized numpy runtime on standard x86_64 CPU.
plots.notes: Sub-millisecond retrieval timings on tiny corpora are subject to microbenchmark timer resolution and cache state variance.

plots.title: Pretrained Model Embedding Latency
plots.purpose: Quantify neural inference overhead for single element, single query, and batched embeddings.
plots.description: Bar chart showing measured CPU execution latency (median) for single code element embedding (11.57ms), query string embedding (9.68ms), and batch of 50 items (40.20ms, ~0.80ms/item amortized).
plots.methodology: Measured using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 transformer model executed on CPU across repeated trials with median reporting.
plots.notes: Batching provides significant throughput improvement for repository-level indexing, while single query inference remains fast (~10ms).

plots.title: Vector Store Memory Scaling
plots.purpose: Demonstrate memory footprint of 384-dimensional dense float32 vector storage as corpus size scales.
plots.description: Line chart showing measured memory footprint in megabytes from 100 to 50,000 code elements (1.55 MB for 1,000 vectors; 77.3 MB for 50,000 vectors).
plots.dataset: Synthetic 384-dimensional dense vectors with metadata headers
plots.methodology: Calculated and verified with 1,536 bytes/vector (384 float32) plus 48 bytes per-element metadata struct.
plots.notes: Memory scaling is strictly linear O(N) and demonstrates that Amoeba can retain tens of thousands of code element vectors in RAM with negligible memory overhead.

plots.title: Measured Brute-Force Retrieval Latency vs. Corpus Size
plots.purpose: Measure brute-force cosine scanning latency across corpus sizes up to 50,000 vectors in the evaluation environment.
plots.description: Line chart displaying measured retrieval scan latency in milliseconds across corpus sizes from 100 to 50,000 vectors against an interactive 10ms threshold line.
plots.methodology: Measured using vectorized dot-product operations on CPU across 100 iterations per corpus size reporting median latency.
plots.notes: Brute-force retrieval remained below 6.4 ms on the measured 50,000-vector benchmark in this environment. ANN/HNSW evaluation is deferred until larger corpora or measured latency requirements justify it.
